guard: a creds source that keeps serving the same generation past its renewal point is refused, so the 60s failure posture applies instead of a 1s re-read loop
why: Adopting an un-re-signed generation re-arms the renewal timer from a non-positive delay, which
armCredsRefresh floors to 1s. The next read returns the same generation, so the loop runs at 1s
for the JWT's remaining life while the 60s CREDS_RETRY_MS backoff is bypassed: the fetch did not
fail, it succeeded and returned nothing new.
The named cell counts source reads inside a fixed window, so it grades the loop itself rather
than the message. The sibling cell asserting the refusal text cannot grade this alone: a future
change could emit that message and still adopt.
The representation half needs its own cell AND its own mutation. A fixture whose source emits one
byte sequence cannot express two representations of one credential, so a green run over it says
nothing about a comparison that is blind to representation.

mutations.name: the un-re-signed generation is adopted instead of refused
mutations.replace: if (current !== undefined && credsFingerprint(candidate) === credsFingerprint(current) && delayMs <= Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY)
mutations.expectRed: an unchanged source past 75% did NOT busy-loop
mutations.cell: an unchanged source past 75% did NOT busy-loop (<=1 renewal read in the churn window)
mutations.note: A finite delay is never <= -Infinity, so the same-generation arm of the guard can never fire: the issue's pre-fix behavior, with the tree compiling and the already-expired arm above it untouched. Under the mutation the cell reported 4 reads against a baseline of 2.

mutations.name: the refusal compares envelope bytes again
mutations.expectRed: a reformatted envelope of the SAME generation is refused, so no 1s re-read follows
mutations.cell: a reformatted envelope of the SAME generation is refused, so no 1s re-read follows
mutations.note: The other conjunct. A two-conjunct predicate needs a mutation per conjunct: the delay mutation above reports a clean kill while leaving the equality comparison entirely ungraded, which is exactly how the byte comparison survived a fully green run. The churn cell stays GREEN under this one - its source returns one exact string, where byte equality and generation equality agree - so the cell that reddens is the reformatted-envelope one.
